name: ci

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

jobs:
  test:
    strategy:
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest]
        node: [20, 22]
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: ${{ matrix.node }}
          cache: npm
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm run typecheck
      - run: npx vitest run

  packed-smoke:
    # Fast PR subset of the exact npm artifact contract. Linux and macOS run
    # the supported lifecycle path; Windows runs the same honest public-CLI
    # subset (install/status/custom-port up+down/hook/MCP/restart/isolation).
    name: packed smoke (${{ matrix.os }})
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest, windows-latest]
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
          cache: npm
      - run: npm ci
      - name: packed tarball smoke
        run: npm run test:packed:smoke
        env:
          MEMWARDEN_PACKED_ARTIFACTS: ${{ runner.temp }}/memwarden-packed-contract
      - name: archive packed-contract failure logs
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: packed-smoke-${{ runner.os }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/memwarden-packed-contract
          if-no-files-found: warn

  firewall-eval:
    # The launch claims, measured on every push: stale-refusal, fresh
    # retention, project isolation, label accuracy — all must hold at 100%.
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
          cache: npm
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm run eval

name: release

# Publish memwarden to npm with provenance when a v* tag is pushed. The full
# source gates and packed-tarball contract on Linux/macOS must pass first — a
# release that skipped what users actually install is not a release.
#
# Setup (one time): configure npm Trusted Publishing for `memwarden`
# (npmjs.com -> package Settings -> Trusted Publisher -> this repo + this
# workflow file), or add an NPM_TOKEN secret. Trusted publishing is preferred:
# no long-lived token, and consumers get source-linked provenance.

on:
  push:
    tags: ["v*"]

jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
          cache: npm
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm run typecheck
      - run: npx vitest run
      # The trust gates. A release that passes unit tests but breaks the
      # firewall would ship a broken CENTRAL promise — so the eval corpus
      # (8 gates at 100%) and the end-to-end demo (real daemon, byte-scan
      # proven erasure, exits non-zero on any broken stage) both block it.
      - run: npm run build
      - name: firewall eval gate
        run: npm run eval
      - name: firewall demo end to end
        run: npm run demo:firewall
      - name: tag must match package.json version
        run: |
          PKG=$(node -p "require('./package.json').version")
          TAG="${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}"
          test "$PKG" = "$TAG" || { echo "tag v$TAG != package.json $PKG"; exit 1; }

  packed-contract:
    # Full installed-artifact journeys block publish on both supported desktop
    # kernels. Linux also exercises the side-loaded TypeScript vector runtime
    # and native turbovec when that optional package exists for the runner.
    name: packed contract (${{ matrix.os }})
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - os: ubuntu-latest
            vectors: "1"
          - os: macos-latest
            vectors: "0"
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    timeout-minutes: 35
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
          cache: npm
      - run: npm ci
      - name: full packed-tarball beta contract
        run: npm run test:packed
        env:
          MEMWARDEN_PACKED_VECTORS: ${{ matrix.vectors }}
          MEMWARDEN_PACKED_ARTIFACTS: ${{ runner.temp }}/memwarden-packed-contract
      - name: archive packed-contract failure logs
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: packed-release-${{ runner.os }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/memwarden-packed-contract
          if-no-files-found: warn

  publish:
    needs: [gate, packed-contract]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      id-token: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      # npm trusted publishing (OIDC) requires Node >=22.14 / npm >=11.5.1.
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22
          registry-url: https://registry.npmjs.org
      - run: npm install -g npm@latest
      - run: npm ci

      # Which auth path will be used, stated before we try it. A silent choice
      # here is why 0.0.6 failed confusingly.
      - name: report auth path
        env:
          NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          if [ -n "$NPM_TOKEN" ]; then
            echo "auth: NPM_TOKEN secret is present — publishing with the token."
            echo "note: a present-but-stale token PREVENTS the OIDC fallback. If this"
            echo "      step 404s, either refresh the token or delete the secret and"
            echo "      configure npm Trusted Publishing for this repo + workflow."
            echo "note: if the account requires 2FA for writes, NO token can work here"
            echo "      (npm demands an OTP, which CI cannot supply). Trusted Publishing"
            echo "      is the only CI-compatible path in that case — and it requires"
            echo "      this secret to be ABSENT."
          else
            echo "auth: no NPM_TOKEN secret — publishing via OIDC trusted publishing."
            echo "note: this requires a trusted publisher configured on npmjs.com for"
            echo "      saiyam1814/memwarden and .github/workflows/release.yml."
          fi

      # NODE_AUTH_TOKEN is set ONLY when the secret is non-empty. Exporting an
      # empty value still makes npm attempt token auth, which shadows OIDC and
      # turns "trusted publishing is configured" into a 404. Keeping the two
      # paths mutually exclusive is what makes either of them work.
      - name: publish
        env:
          NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          set -o pipefail
          if [ -n "$NPM_TOKEN" ]; then
            export NODE_AUTH_TOKEN="$NPM_TOKEN"
          fi
          if ! npm publish --provenance --access public 2>&1 | tee publish.log; then
            if grep -q "EOTP\|one-time password" publish.log; then
              echo "::error::npm accepted the token but demands a one-time password (EOTP)."
              echo "::error::The account has 2FA required for writes, and CI can NEVER supply an OTP."
              echo "::error::A token cannot fix this. Use Trusted Publishing instead:"
              echo "::error::  1. npmjs.com -> package 'memwarden' -> Settings -> Trusted Publisher"
              echo "::error::     GitHub Actions | org saiyam1814 | repo memwarden | release.yml"
              echo "::error::  2. gh secret delete NPM_TOKEN   (its presence blocks the OIDC path)"
              echo "::error::  3. re-run this workflow"
              echo "::error::OIDC is exempt from OTP because the workflow identity is attested,"
              echo "::error::so this is the only CI-compatible option short of weakening 2FA."
            elif grep -q "E404\|404 Not Found - PUT" publish.log; then
              echo "::error::npm rejected the credentials for this package (E404 on PUT)."
              echo "::error::The package exists, so this is an AUTH failure, not a missing name."
              if [ -n "$NPM_TOKEN" ]; then
                echo "::error::Fix: refresh NPM_TOKEN with a granular token that has publish"
                echo "::error::rights on 'memwarden', OR delete the NPM_TOKEN secret and"
                echo "::error::configure Trusted Publishing so this workflow authenticates by OIDC."
              else
                echo "::error::Fix: configure a trusted publisher on npmjs.com for"
                echo "::error::saiyam1814/memwarden with workflow .github/workflows/release.yml."
              fi
            fi
            exit 1
          fi

name: turbovec-release

# Prebuild @memwarden/turbovec for every supported platform and publish ONE
# npm package containing all binaries (the package.json files field includes
# *.node; memwarden's loader picks the right one via napi's index.js).
#
# Trigger: push a tag like turbovec-v0.1.0, or run manually. Publishing needs
# either npm Trusted Publishing configured for @memwarden/turbovec (preferred:
# repo Settings on npmjs.com -> Trusted Publisher -> this repo + this workflow
# file) or an NPM_TOKEN secret with publish rights to the @memwarden scope.

on:
  push:
    tags: ["turbovec-v*"]
  workflow_dispatch: {}

defaults:
  run:
    working-directory: native/turbovec-node

jobs:
  build:
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          # macOS links the system Accelerate framework (always present), so it
          # builds natively on the runner. Linux x64 builds inside the old-glibc
          # node:20-bullseye container (glibc 2.31, broad compatibility) and
          # STATICALLY links an OpenBLAS compiled from source (no runtime BLAS,
          # no fortran runtime dependency).
          #
          # Linux ARM64 is intentionally NOT a native prebuild: OpenBLAS's
          # Neoverse kernels fail to compile under bullseye's gcc, and forcing a
          # newer compiler would raise the glibc floor. arm64 Linux users get
          # the honest TypeScript fallback (memwarden status names the real
          # backend) until a clean arm64 build path lands. Tracked as a follow-up.
          - host: macos-14
            target: aarch64-apple-darwin
          # macos-13 (the last free Intel image) was retired in Dec 2025;
          # macos-15-intel is GitHub's designated replacement.
          - host: macos-15-intel
            target: x86_64-apple-darwin
          - host: ubuntu-latest
            target: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
            buildImage: node:20-bullseye
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.host }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          targets: ${{ matrix.target }}
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          workspaces: native/turbovec-node
      # Linux: build in the old-glibc napi-rs container so the .node runs on a
      # broad range of distros (bullseye glibc, well below node:20-slim's).
      # openblas-src compiles OpenBLAS in-container, statically linked, so the
      # binary references only the container's (old) glibc and no runtime BLAS.
      - name: build binding (linux — portable old-glibc container)
        if: contains(matrix.target, 'linux')
        working-directory: .
        run: |
          docker run --rm -v "$PWD":/w -w /w/native/turbovec-node ${{ matrix.buildImage }} \
            bash -lc '
              set -e
              # node:20-bullseye has node + build tools + curl; add gfortran for
              # the openblas-src static compile and a current Rust via rustup
              # (bullseye repos ship no rustc). Old glibc (2.31) stays, so the
              # binary loads broadly; the toolchain version is independent of it.
              apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends gfortran make gcc g++ perl
              curl --proto "=https" --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh -s -- -y --default-toolchain stable --profile minimal
              . "$HOME/.cargo/env"
              npm ci
              npx napi build --release --platform --target ${{ matrix.target }}
            '
      # macOS: build natively (Accelerate is in the OS).
      - name: build binding (macos)
        if: ${{ !contains(matrix.target, 'linux') }}
        run: |
          npm ci
          npx napi build --release --platform --target ${{ matrix.target }}
      # Per-platform gate: the freshly built binding must pass memwarden's
      # real native integration tests on THIS platform before it ships.
      - name: test the binding on this platform
        working-directory: .
        run: |
          npm ci
          npx vitest run test/turbovec-native.test.ts
      # The PROMOTION BENCHMARK the docs advertise: recall drop <= 2 points
      # vs FP32, in-kernel allowlist correctness, add/remove/save/load id-set
      # parity. This is what makes the "auto" default honest — a published
      # binary is a binary that passed this gate on its platform.
      - name: promotion benchmark gate
        working-directory: .
        run: npm run benchmark:backends
      # CLEAN-CONSUMER gate: the binding must dlopen in a bare node:20-slim
      # image — no OpenBLAS, no build tools, and a stock glibc — or it must
      # not ship. This catches both a dynamic libopenblas dependency and a
      # too-new glibc requirement before either reaches a user.
      - name: clean-container load test (linux)
        if: contains(matrix.target, 'linux')
        run: |
          docker run --rm -v "$PWD":/pkg -w /pkg node:20-slim \
            node -e "const b = require('./index.js'); const k = Object.keys(b); if (k.length === 0) throw new Error('no exports'); console.log('clean-container load OK:', k.join(','));"
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: binding-${{ matrix.target }}
          path: native/turbovec-node/*.node
          if-no-files-found: error

  # NOTE: auto-publish removed. This workflow BUILDS + VALIDATES the native
  # binding for every platform (build, native tests, promotion benchmark, and
  # the clean-container load gate) and uploads each platform's *.node as an
  # artifact. Publishing is done manually — download the artifacts from a green
  # run and `npm publish` locally (an interactive OTP works; CI cannot provide
  # one). See docs/RELEASE-turbovec.md. Once the package exists on npm,
  # configure Trusted Publishing (OIDC) and this can auto-publish token-free.

{
  "name": "memwarden",
  "version": "0.2.0",
  "description": "Memory for AI coding agents that checks itself against your code. A memory whose source files changed is refused, not recalled. Local, shared by all your agents, tamper-evident.",
  "type": "module",
  "engines": {
    "node": ">=20.0.0"
  },
  "bin": {
    "memwarden": "dist/cli/bin.js",
    "memwarden-mcp": "dist/mcp/bin.js"
  },
  "files": [
    "dist",
    "README.md",
    "LICENSE"
  ],
  "repository": {
    "type": "git",
    "url": "git+https://github.com/saiyam1814/memwarden.git"
  },
  "homepage": "https://github.com/saiyam1814/memwarden#readme",
  "bugs": {
    "url": "https://github.com/saiyam1814/memwarden/issues"
  },
  "keywords": [
    "ai",
    "memory",
    "agents",
    "mcp",
    "claude-code",
    "verified-recall",
    "memory-firewall",
    "local-first"
  ],
  "scripts": {
    "dev": "tsx src/index.ts",
    "build": "tsc",
    "prepack": "npm run build",
    "benchmark": "tsx benchmark/recall.ts",
    "benchmark:backends": "tsx benchmark/backends.ts",
    "demo:trust": "tsx demo/trust.ts",
    "test": "vitest run",
    "test:watch": "vitest",
    "test:packed:smoke": "node test/packed-beta-contract.mjs --profile=smoke",
    "test:packed": "node test/packed-beta-contract.mjs --profile=full",
    "typecheck": "tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.eval.json",
    "demo:firewall": "tsx demo/firewall.ts",
    "eval": "tsx eval/firewall-eval.ts",
    "eval:halflife": "tsx eval/memory-halflife.ts",
    "eval:halflife:artifact": "tsx eval/memory-halflife-artifact.ts",
    "inspect": "tsx eval/inspect-store.ts"
  },
  "license": "Apache-2.0",
  "dependencies": {
    "@libsql/client": "^0.15.0",
    "zod": "^4.0.0"
  },
  "devDependencies": {
    "@huggingface/transformers": "^3.8.1",
    "@types/node": "^25.9.1",
    "tsx": "^4.19.0",
    "typescript": "^6.0.3",
    "vitest": "^4.1.6"
  },
  "author": ""
}

#
# memwarden canon verify — a memory-trust gate for pull requests.
#
# Every orchestrator, agent team, and parallel-agent workflow eventually
# converges on a pull request, which makes CI the one place that can check
# memory trust regardless of which tools produced it. This action re-hashes the
# committed .memwarden/canon.jsonl against the PR's checkout and reports which
# memories no longer hold.
#
# It needs no daemon, no account, and no secrets: verification is a local
# re-hash of files that are already in the checkout.
#
#   - uses: saiyam1814/memwarden@main
#     with:
#       strict: 'true'   # fail the job when a memory references changed code
#
name: memwarden canon verify
description: Verify committed agent memory still holds against this checkout (re-hashes source files; no daemon, no secrets).
author: memwarden
branding:
  icon: shield
  color: red

inputs:
  root:
    description: Repository root to verify (defaults to the workspace).
    required: false
    default: .
  strict:
    description: Fail the job when any memory is stale. Set 'false' to report without failing.
    required: false
    default: "true"
  version:
    description: memwarden version to run (npm dist-tag or exact version).
    required: false
    default: latest
  summary:
    description: Write the verdict to the GitHub step summary.
    required: false
    default: "true"

outputs:
  verified:
    description: Number of memories that still hold against this checkout.
    value: ${{ steps.verify.outputs.verified }}
  stale:
    description: Number of memories referencing code that changed or vanished.
    value: ${{ steps.verify.outputs.stale }}
  total:
    description: Total records in the canon.
    value: ${{ steps.verify.outputs.total }}

runs:
  using: composite
  steps:
    - name: verify canon
      id: verify
      shell: bash
      env:
        MW_ROOT: ${{ inputs.root }}
        MW_STRICT: ${{ inputs.strict }}
        MW_VERSION: ${{ inputs.version }}
        MW_SUMMARY: ${{ inputs.summary }}
      run: |
        set -uo pipefail

        # No canon committed is not a failure: most repos adopting this action
        # add the workflow before they add the file.
        if [ ! -f "$MW_ROOT/.memwarden/canon.jsonl" ]; then
          echo "no .memwarden/canon.jsonl in $MW_ROOT — nothing to verify."
          echo "create one on a machine with memory: memwarden canon push"
          {
            echo "verified=0"; echo "stale=0"; echo "total=0"
          } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          exit 0
        fi

        # --json so the verdict is parsed, never scraped from prose.
        npx --yes "memwarden@$MW_VERSION" canon verify --root "$MW_ROOT" --json > mw-canon.json
        cat mw-canon.json

        read -r TOTAL VERIFIED STALE UNVER < <(node -e '
          const r = require("./mw-canon.json");
          process.stdout.write([r.total ?? 0, r.verified ?? 0, r.stale ?? 0, r.unverifiable ?? 0].join(" "));
        ')
        {
          echo "verified=$VERIFIED"; echo "stale=$STALE"; echo "total=$TOTAL"
        } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

        if [ "$MW_SUMMARY" = "true" ]; then
          {
            echo "## memwarden canon verify"
            echo
            echo "| verdict | count |"
            echo "| --- | --- |"
            echo "| verified | $VERIFIED |"
            echo "| stale | $STALE |"
            echo "| unverifiable | $UNVER |"
            echo
            if [ "$STALE" != "0" ]; then
              echo "### Stale memories"
              echo
              node -e '
                const r = require("./mw-canon.json");
                for (const s of (r.staleDetail ?? []).slice(0, 20)) {
                  console.log("- **" + s.title + "** — drifted: `" + (s.drifted ?? []).join("`, `") + "`");
                }
              '
              echo
              echo "These memories reference code this branch changed. They are refused at"
              echo "recall rather than injected, so nothing is silently wrong — but the canon"
              echo "should be refreshed (\`memwarden canon push\`) or the dead records dropped."
            else
              echo "Every committed memory still hash-matches this checkout."
              echo
              echo "_A matching hash proves the source is unchanged, not that the claim is correct._"
            fi
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
        fi

        if [ "$MW_STRICT" = "true" ] && [ "$STALE" != "0" ]; then
          echo "::error::$STALE committed memories reference code this branch changed."
          exit 1
        fi

# napi-rs binding around the turbovec crate's IdMapIndex. Built as a Node
# addon (cdylib); see README.md for the build command. This crate is a thin
# FFI shim: all vector math lives in turbovec, all id-string mapping lives in
# memwarden's TypeScript loader (src/functions/turbovec-backend.ts).

[package]
name = "memwarden-turbovec"
version = "0.1.5"
edition = "2021"
license = "MIT"
description = "Node bindings for turbovec::IdMapIndex (memwarden's optional native vector backend)"
repository = "https://github.com/saiyam1814/memwarden"

[lib]
crate-type = ["cdylib"]

[dependencies]
# napi6 is required for BigInt <-> u64 argument conversion (external ids).
napi = { version = "2", default-features = false, features = ["napi6"] }
napi-derive = "2"
turbovec = "0.9"

# --- BLAS backend ---------------------------------------------------------
# turbovec pulls in ndarray with the `blas` feature (not toggleable from
# here), which needs a cblas implementation. On macOS that resolves to the
# always-present Accelerate framework, so the binary is self-contained with
# no extra work. On Linux the default resolves to a DYNAMIC libopenblas.so.0
# that a user's machine won't have (the clean-container CI gate caught this).
# So on Linux we STATICALLY link OpenBLAS (built from vendored source by
# openblas-src) and pull it in via blas-src + `extern crate blas_src` in
# lib.rs — the .node then has no external BLAS NEEDED and loads anywhere.
[target.'cfg(target_os = "linux")'.dependencies]
blas-src = { version = "0.10", default-features = false, features = ["openblas"] }
openblas-src = { version = "0.10", default-features = false, features = ["cblas", "lapacke", "static"] }

[build-dependencies]
napi-build = "2"

[profile.release]
lto = true
strip = "symbols"

### The memory firewall for AI coding agents **Code changes. Stored memory can outlive its source. Expose the drift.** Memory whose source no longer checks out is **blocked before it reaches the model** - and everything that passes is labeled for exactly what it is. [![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/memwarden?color=FF4D6A&label=npm&logo=npm&logoColor=white)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/memwarden) [![CI](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/saiyam1814/memwarden/ci.yml?branch=main&label=CI&logo=github)](https://github.com/saiyam1814/memwarden/actions) [![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache--2.0-FF4D6A)](LICENSE) [![node](https://img.shields.io/badge/node-%E2%89%A520-339933?logo=node.js&logoColor=white)](package.json) [![stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/saiyam1814/memwarden?style=flat&color=FF4D6A)](https://github.com/saiyam1814/memwarden) ```bash npx memwarden audit # zero-install: audit the memory you already have npm install -g memwarden && memwarden up # persistent: wire every agent, one command ``` [Quick start](#-quick-start) · [Why](#-why-memwarden) · [Trust states](#-the-five-trust-states) · [Compatibility](#-compatibility) · [How it works](#-how-it-works) · [Docs](#-docs)
--- memwarden is **self-custodied, verified memory** shared across every coding agent you use - Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Kiro, OpenCode, and more. The point isn't to remember *more*. It's that a coding agent can settle a question general-purpose memory can't: **does this memory's recorded source still match?** Every code-backed memory is tied to a SHA-256 hash of the files it references; on recall the live repo is re-hashed, and anything that no longer checks out is refused before the model ever sees it. ## 🚀 Quick start ```bash npm install -g memwarden memwarden up ``` `memwarden up` is the whole setup. It: - starts a **self-healing daemon** - one brain at `~/.memwarden`, registered as a launchd / systemd service - installs **on-device embeddings** (all-MiniLM-L6-v2) so recall is semantic from day one - nothing leaves the machine - writes the **MCP server + native hooks** into every installed tool, in each tool's own config, without clobbering anything - ends by printing `memwarden status` so you can see it's flowing `memwarden down --all` reverses everything it wrote; `--data` deletes the brain. Prefer to try before you install? `npx memwarden audit ` needs no daemon and no setup. macOS launchd and POSIX detached daemon logs are owner-only (`0600`) and checked every minute: each oversized current log is reduced in place while at most one 1 MiB tail is retained as `daemon.log.1`; systemd continues to use journald's own rotation. Windows retains its v0.1.0 detached logging lifecycle, so these POSIX mode and launchd-style rotation guarantees do not apply there. **Already have memory elsewhere?** `memwarden adopt ` seeds an existing CLAUDE.md, claude-mem db, or Mem0 export into the brain so it flows across your agents. Adopted memory carries no capture-time hashes, so it is labeled `sourced` (drift-aware but not content-`verified`) - honest by construction; only memory captured going forward earns `verified`. That drift exposure is not proof the memory is wrong; it is the risk unchecked layers carry when they inject without looking. Every `full`, `compact`, and `narrative` search result carries `trust`, `source_status`, capture time, and an evidence summary. **`balanced`** (default) current recall blocks source-drifted/unverifiable records and keeps verified, cosmetic-current, sourced, and unsourced records labeled - "not detected stale" is not "proven safe." **`verified-only`** raises the current/automatic recall floor to raw-verified or normalized-content-current memory (for hostile-repo threat models); the label still distinguishes them. `memwarden status` reports total **memories served** plus the nonzero verified/cosmetic/sourced/unsourced breakdown; old aggregate-only counters remain explicitly legacy/unclassified. The [versioned JSON contract](docs/configuration.md#firewall-activity-schema) is shared by `/stats` and `status --json`. MCP `memory_search` is project-scoped with `mode: "current"` by default. `mode: "historical"` deliberately returns only source-drifted or superseded records, framed with capture time and evidence; `mode: "all"` (or `include_drifted: true`) is the explicit current+history view. `all_projects: true` checks each hit against its own known checkout; if that checkout is unavailable, the hit is labeled `unverifiable` and is not included as current context. Historical/all inspection bypasses the current inclusion floor, never classification or labels. # @memwarden/turbovec

Node bindings (napi-rs) for the [turbovec](https://github.com/RyanCodrai/turbovec)
Rust crate — memwarden's **optional** native vector backend.

turbovec implements TurboQuant vector quantization (2-4 bits per coordinate,
data-oblivious, no codebook training) with SIMD search kernels (NEON on ARM,
AVX-512/AVX2 on x86). This package wraps its `IdMapIndex` — stable external
`u64` ids, `O(1)` remove, allowlist-masked search, validated `.tvim`
persistence (format v3) — as a Node addon.

## Relationship to memwarden

memwarden's core ships with **zero native dependencies** and never lists this
package as a dependency. At boot, when `MEMWARDEN_VECTOR_BACKEND=turbovec` is
set, memwarden dynamic-imports `@memwarden/turbovec` (first the bare
specifier, then `<dataDir>/runtime/node_modules`). If the import fails, it
logs the reason and serves search from the portable TypeScript index instead
— `memwarden status` and `GET /memwarden/stats` always report which engine is
actually active (`turbovec/native-4bit` vs `typescript/turboquant-4bit`).

The string-obsId to u64 mapping, the persistence envelope and all fallback
logic live in memwarden (`src/functions/turbovec-backend.ts`); this package
is a thin, panic-guarded FFI shim.

## API

```js
const { TurbovecIndex } = require("@memwarden/turbovec");

const idx = new TurbovecIndex(384, 4);        // dims (multiple of 8), bitWidth 2|3|4
idx.addWithIds(f32Buffer, new BigUint64Array([1n, 2n, 3n]));
idx.remove(2n);                                // O(1), returns bool
const { ids, scores } = idx.search(query, 10); // ids: BigUint64Array, best first
idx.search(query, 10, new BigUint64Array([1n])); // allowlist-masked
idx.save("index.tvim");
const loaded = TurbovecIndex.load("index.tvim");
idx.len; idx.dims; idx.bitWidth;
```

The two panic paths documented on the crate's `search_with_allowlist` (empty
allowlist, allowlist id not in the index) are guarded at the FFI boundary:
unknown ids are filtered out and an effectively empty allowlist returns an
empty result — JS callers cannot crash the process through the mask.

The allowlist is wired into production search: when `mem::search` carries a
project/cwd filter, it builds the in-scope obsId set and calls
`TurbovecBackend.searchAllowed`, which translates it to this native u64 mask,
so the scope restriction runs inside the SIMD scan instead of post-filtering
a global top-k (see `benchmark/backends.ts`, filtered-search scenario and
GATE 4).

## Building from source

Requires a Rust toolchain (1.70+) and Node 20+.

```sh
cd native/turbovec-node
npm install          # installs @napi-rs/cli (devDependency of THIS package only)
npm run build        # cargo build --release + generates index.js / index.d.ts
```

This produces `memwarden-turbovec.<platform>.node` (e.g.
`memwarden-turbovec.darwin-arm64.node`). The binary is gitignored — it is
always rebuilt from source or shipped as a CI prebuild.

BLAS linkage (turbovec pulls in `ndarray`'s `blas` feature): macOS resolves
to the system **Accelerate** framework, so the binary is self-contained with
no extra deps. **Linux statically links OpenBLAS** — `openblas-src` builds it
from vendored source (needs a Fortran toolchain: `gfortran make gcc perl`)
and `blas-src` + `extern crate blas_src` route ndarray to it, so the shipped
`.node` has no runtime `libopenblas.so` dependency and loads on a bare
machine. A CI clean-container gate (no OpenBLAS installed) enforces this.

## Prebuild CI matrix

| Target | Status |
| --- | --- |
| `aarch64-apple-darwin` (darwin-arm64) | build + test + benchmark + publish prebuild |
| `x86_64-apple-darwin` (darwin-x64) | build + test + benchmark + publish prebuild |
| `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` (linux-x64 gnu) | build (old-glibc container, static OpenBLAS) + test + benchmark + clean-container gate + publish prebuild |
| `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu` (linux-arm64 gnu) | **not built yet** — OpenBLAS's Neoverse kernels fail to compile under the old-glibc toolchain; TypeScript fallback until a clean arm64 path lands |
| Windows | **not built** — TypeScript fallback |

memwarden's `auto` backend loads the native engine wherever its prebuilt
binary is present and honestly falls back to TypeScript otherwise
(`memwarden status` names the backend actually serving), so unshipped targets
are correct-everywhere, just not accelerated.

Each prebuild job must run the full `test/turbovec-native.test.ts` suite and
`npm run benchmark:backends` (the promotion gate) against its artifact.
musl targets are out of scope until someone needs them; they fall back to
TypeScript like every other unsupported platform.

## How the "auto" default stays honest

memwarden's default backend mode is `auto`: the native engine is selected
whenever this binding actually loads, and the portable TypeScript index
serves otherwise. That is honest because a published `@memwarden/turbovec`
binary is one that passed, in CI, on its own platform: the integration
tests, the promotion benchmark (recall drop <= 2 points vs FP32, allowlist
purity, add/remove/save/load id-set parity), and — on Linux — a
clean-container load test with no OpenBLAS installed. Pin a backend
explicitly per environment:

```sh
MEMWARDEN_VECTOR_BACKEND=turbovec   # or: typescript
```

A failed native load is never silent and never lies about the label —
`memwarden status` always names the backend actually serving. (On
darwin-arm64 the native engine measures p50 0.15 ms vs 18.9 ms per search
over 10K vectors at identical 1-recall@10.)
